page.overview:
What is herbology?

Herbology was the study of all plants and fungi, magical and mundane. Wizards and witches who specialised in this field were known as Herbologists.

The study of Herbology encompassed a vast array of topics, ranging from the mundane to the magical. Herbologists explored the growth patterns of magical plants, their preferred habitats, cultivation techniques, and the effects of magical properties on their surroundings. They also studied the uses of these plants in potion-making.

There were a vast variety of magic plants and fungi in the wizarding world, each with its unique properties and characteristics. Throughout wizarding history, herbology has been shaped by the contributions of notable figures. A Herbologist and author, Phyllida Spore, wrote the Herbology textbook One Thousand Magical Herbs and Fungi.

The knowledge gleaned from Herbology had practical applications in various magical endeavours. Most prominent was their use in potions. The Mandrake for example was the essential ingredient in the Mandrake Restorative Draught. According to Professor Aesop Sharp, Herbology class was just as important to the learning of potions as Potions class itself. It was good to have a solid grasp on not only how to combine ingredients, but to have an understanding of the ingredients themselves. The plants nurtured in Herbology class were often essential in potions. Being able to source one's own potion ingredients also helped to save a Galleon or two.
